name: Lechweg
kurzbeschreibung: The Lechweg begins at Formarinsee at 1,793 m on the Arlberg: Europe's first Leading Quality Trail, origin of the Lech, and pristine high-alpine nature.
preis: Wanderweg kostenlos; Wanderbus Formarinsee ca. 15,00 € (mit Lech Card frei)
oeffnungszeiten: Mitte Juni bis Anfang Okt frei zugänglich (schneefrei)
beschreibung:
Overview

The Lechweg is one of the most prestigious and visually captivating long-distance hiking trails in Europe. It originates in the high-alpine headwaters of the Lech at the picturesque Formarinsee at an altitude of 1,793 metres above sea level near Lech am Arlberg, following the last wild river of the Northern Limestone Alps over roughly 125 kilometres down to the Lechfall near Füssen. As the very first long-distance hiking trail ever, the Lechweg was awarded the coveted “Leading Quality Trail – Best of Europe” certification by the European Ramblers' Association. The alpine opening leg on the Arlberg guides hikers through an untouched high-mountain landscape of breathtaking beauty.

From Formarinsee through the Arlberg Region

The official starting point at emerald-green Formarinsee is nestled beneath the immense rock face of the Rote Wand (2,704 m) in the Lechquellen Mountains—in 2015, this area was voted Austria's most beautiful spot by television viewers. Here, close to the Formarinalpe, springs the Formarinbach, which merges a few kilometres down the valley with the Spullerbach to form the young Lech. The initial stages of the long-distance trail lead from the Formarinalpe along close-to-nature paths flanking the crystal-clear mountain stream through the idyllic Zugertal to the world-renowned gourmet village of Lech am Arlberg (1,444 m). The route then continues across blooming alpine pastures and through airy mountain forests to Warth am Arlberg, before crossing the border into the Tyrolean Lechtal. Along the trail, hikers discover historic Walser settlements, traditional wooden alpine dairies, and unique geological oddities such as the bizarre gypsum sinkholes (Gipslöcher) near Lech.

Visit & Getting There

The optimal hiking season for the alpine sections of the Lechweg on the Arlberg extends from mid-June to early October (outside this period, elevations above 1,700 m are frequently blanketed in snow). Walking the trail is free and completely open to the public. Luggage transport services (hotel-to-hotel) and dedicated Lechweg shuttles allow for carefree trekking. Arrival by car: take the Arlbergschnellstraße S16 to Langen am Arlberg, continuing via the Flexenpass (L198) to Zürs and Lech am Arlberg; in summer, a toll hiking bus transports visitors directly from Lech to Formarinsee. By public transport: take ÖBB trains to Bahnhof Langen am Arlberg, and connect with frequent Postbus routes 750/760 directly to Lech am Arlberg (Rüfiplatz).

Tips

The initial stages demand sturdy mountain hiking boots, surefootedness, and weatherproof clothing; telescopic trekking poles are highly recommended for the alpine descents. Overnight accommodations in Lech, Zug, and Warth should be booked well in advance during peak summer months. With the regional Lech Card, summer guests enjoy complimentary access to local village buses and summer cable cars throughout the Arlberg region.
